newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight rates edge up in tight market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight rates edge up in tight market.

text.p: Manila's overnight rates edged up for the second day this week due to a temporary drain on liquidity from tax payments and dollar buying in the previous days, traders said on Tuesday.
"Some major banks are still feeling the pinch of a tight market so they are borrowing funds from other banks," said one dealer. The average rate inched up to 11.59375 percent from Monday's 11.09375.
The overnight rates peaked at 12.5 percent after two big banks borrowed money in the market.
Among the lenders were a government-controlled bank, traders said.
Total volume slipped to 23.282 billion pesos from the previous 28.278 billion. There were 27 borrowers and 33 lenders in the market.
Traders said they expected rates to remain steady to higher for the rest of the week.
Secondary trading of government securities was active for the one-year bills and quiet for other maturities.
A Reuters survey of seven banks indicated three-months bills were being bid at 11.525 to 11.65 percent and offered at 11.4 to 11.5 percent.

Bids for six-month bills ranged between 11.85 to 12 percent and offered at 11.725 to 11.825 percent while bids for one-year bills ranged between 12.25 and 12.375 percent and offered at 12.1 to 12.25 percent.
Traders said they expected the coupon rate for two-year notes at this afternoon's auction by the Department of finance to soften to 13.125 percent from the previous month's 13.75.
